personal.intro: I build LLM systems and the plumbing that keeps them standing: retrieval over messy documents, multi-agent workflows, and the routers, queues and budgets underneath. Everything below is running somewhere.

projects.title: Agentic App Builder
projects.description: Describe an app in a sentence and four LLM agents — planner, developer, tester, reviewer — pass it around a LangGraph state machine until the code passes its own tests. The result boots in a sandboxed subprocess behind a reverse proxy that feeds browser console errors back into the loop. Five runtimes: Python, Node, React, Angular, static.

projects.title: Model Fallback Router
projects.kicker: When the model you wanted is down
projects.description: Sits in front of your LLM providers. When one starts failing or breaches its latency SLA, a circuit breaker trips and traffic moves to the next model in the chain. The dashboard shows which model actually served each request.

projects.title: Async Inference Queue
projects.description: A Redis-backed priority queue for LLM jobs. Workers pull by priority, backpressure kicks in before the queue runs away, and anything that exhausts its retries lands in a dead-letter queue you can actually inspect.

projects.title: Token Cost Budget Dashboard
projects.description: Prices each LLM call and attributes it to a team and a project. When a budget is spent the next request is refused rather than quietly billed. Works with any provider LiteLLM speaks to. 40 tests.

projects.title: RAG Eval Suite
projects.description: Scores a RAG pipeline on faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and recall with RAGAS, so a retrieval tweak stops being a matter of opinion. Local sentence-transformers embeddings, ChromaDB behind it, FastAPI in front.

projects.title: Agent Tool Calls & Retries
projects.kicker: A ReAct loop that survives a flaky tool
projects.description: A ReAct loop built on native function calling, with exponential backoff when a tool fails and a JSON trace of every step the agent took. Swap the model without touching the agent. Ships LangGraph, CrewAI and Google A2A adapters. 31 tests.

projects.title: Carbon Calculator Platform
projects.kicker: Lifecycle carbon for a laptop fleet
projects.description: Works out the lifecycle carbon of a laptop fleet: ingests vendor spec data, applies country-level grid emission factors, and gives people comparison dashboards, with admin controls behind role-based access.

projects.title: GenAI Roadmap
projects.description: A mobile-first study companion for working through the GenAI roadmap — structure and progress tracking on the device you actually have on you.

about.profile: Gen AI Consultant at Atos, five years in. I moved from cloud and full-stack delivery into building generative AI for enterprises, which in practice means the unphotogenic half: long-context retrieval over real documents that were never meant to be parsed, multi-agent workflows with schema enforcement and fault tolerance, and OCR-plus-LLM pipelines accurate enough to write into an ERP. I still build the stack around it — Java, Spring Boot, Node.js, Angular, Python — and ship it on GCP and AWS with Docker, Kubernetes and GitHub Actions.

experience.title: Gen AI Consultant
points: Built a long-context RAG system over course material — PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX — that checks it against a data-quality checklist and files the compliance report to SharePoint. Review time down 65%.
Shipped an accounts-receivable email agent that classifies mail, pulls invoice data out of the attachments and validates it before anyone sees it. Resolution time down 55%.
Built the pipeline underneath: OCR with pdfplumber and pytesseract, Llama-3 prompting, then an agent validation pass. 96% field-level accuracy, ERP-ready JSON out.
Orchestrated it on LangGraph and MCP with separate retrieval, validation, synthesis and orchestration agents, schema enforcement and fault tolerance throughout.
Ran the delivery side too: Docker, Kubernetes and GitHub Actions onto GCP and AWS, plus Angular and Node.js migrations off the legacy architecture.
